original_question: For each 1 <= p < infinity, decide whether the bounded compact approximation constant M(H^p) is equal to the operator norm of the map f -> f - f_hat(0) on H^p(T), equivalently whether M(H^p) = ||I - K_0||_{B(H^p)}, where K_0 is the Fejer operator at n = 0.
target_in_paper: Section 5.3, immediately after Open problem 5.5(a): the follow-up remark asking whether the exact BCAP constant M(H^p) might equal ||I-K_0||_{B(H^p)}; with Section 5.2 / Open problem 5.4 supplying the explicit backward-shift reformulation of the n=0 case.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the classical Hardy space H^p with range 1 ≤ p < ∞, the specific operator I-K_0 (equivalently the map sending f to f minus its constant term), and the paper’s narrow follow-up question about whether the exact BCAP constant for H^p coincides with that operator norm.
missing_details: The draft does not define the BCAP approximation constant M(H^p): it is the infimum of all M such that for every ε > 0 and every finite F ⊂ H^p there exists a compact operator T on H^p with ||I-T|| ≤ M and ||f-Tf|| < ε for all f in F.
It should state explicitly that H^p means the classical Hardy space H[L^p(𝕋)] on the unit circle 𝕋 with normalized Lebesgue measure, as in the paper’s setup.
K_0 should be defined precisely as the zeroth Fejér operator; in this case K_0 f is the constant function equal to the zeroth Fourier coefficient of f.
The operator norm should be explicitly taken in the Banach algebra B(H^p).

The paper does not present this as a numbered conjecture or open problem by itself; it appears as a follow-up remark immediately after the broader labeled Open problem 5.5(a), which asks for the exact value of M(H^p).
The paper’s explicit alternate formulation is via the backward shift operator in Section 5.2; that equivalence should be mentioned if one wants the sharpest paper-faithful stand-alone version.

A subtle but important paper-faithfulness point is that the motivating comparison is the known identity for the alternative approximation constant m(L^p), not for M(L^p); the draft omits this distinction.
refined_question: For the classical Hardy space H^p = H[L^p(𝕋)] on the unit circle 𝕋 with normalized Lebesgue measure, and for each 1 ≤ p < ∞, is its bounded compact approximation constant M(H^p)—that is, the infimum of all M > 0 such that for every ε > 0 and every finite set F ⊂ H^p there exists a compact operator T on H^p with ||I-T|| ≤ M and ||f-Tf|| < ε for all f ∈ F—equal to ||I-K_0||_{B(H^p)}, where K_0 is the zeroth Fejér operator (so K_0f is the constant function given by the zeroth Fourier coefficient of f, and therefore (I-K_0)f is f with its constant term removed)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the standard identification of boundary and analytic Hardy spaces, for each 1 ≤ p < ∞, is M(H^p) equal to the operator norm of the backward shift B on H^p, where Bf(z) = (f(z)-f(0))/z?
justification: This draft does not target Theorem 1.3 itself, and this paper has no Conjecture 1.1 or Proposition 1.2; it clearly targets the open-problem discussion in Section 5. More precisely, the paper first asks in Open problem 5.5(a) for the exact value of M(H^p), 1 ≤ p < ∞, and then immediately adds the narrower remark matching your draft: motivated by the known formula for the alternative approximation constant m(L^p) in terms of I-K_0 from the introduction, the authors ask whether the Hardy-space BCAP constant M(H^p) might equal ||I-K_0||. Section 5.2 separately isolates the n = 0 case as the exact norm of the backward shift operator, so the only paper-explicit alternate formulation is the backward-shift version.
